description: One disclosure a filing has to make, and whether it has been made. NOT APPLICABLE IS A COMPLETED STATE AND OUTSTANDING IS NOT — the whole value of a checklist is that somebody decided about every line, and 'we have no segments to report' is a decision while an empty row is an omission. The two must never look the same.

fields.description: What has to be disclosed — 'Related party transactions', 'Subsequent events', 'Going concern assessment'. The item's key, and what a completion names.
fields.label: Disclosure Item

fields.description: OUTSTANDING is the only state the completeness control counts as a gap. `Not Applicable` is completed — somebody looked and decided — and `In Progress` is honest about work started, but neither is Outstanding and neither blocks a filing.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Outstanding
In Progress
Complete
Not Applicable

fields.description: Whether the filing can be finalised without it. An optional item left outstanding is a choice; a required one is what the control refuses on.
fields.label: Required

fields.description: The item in Spanish, for a preparer who works in it. Empty means English is served and the gap is reported rather than hidden.
fields.label: Item (ES)

fields.description: What requires it — 'ASC 850', 'Reg S-K Item 303', 'SOX §302 certification'. This is the column an auditor reads first.
fields.label: Requirement Reference

fields.description: Who owes this one. The commonest reason a disclosure is omitted is not refusal — it is that nobody was assigned.
fields.label: Assigned To

fields.description: Where the disclosure actually is — the working paper, the note number, the tool that produced it ('generate_related_party_disclosure'). A completed item that points at nothing is a tick.
fields.label: Evidence Reference

fields.description: For a Not Applicable, this is where the reason goes — and the reason is the disclosure.
fields.label: Notes

name: Disclosure Checklist Item
